one_liner: Administrative operations generalist at ICE handling budget, procurement, HR, property, space, travel, and fleet management support for an office, advising managers on improvements.
fit_summary: Daniel's consulting work for government clients at IEM and strong interpersonal and policy skills align with the briefings, management advice, and customer-service parts of this role. However, the core duties are hands-on administrative operations (budget, procurement, property, fleet), and qualifying at GS-11 requires a full year of GS-09-equivalent specialized experience that Daniel must document clearly. GS-11 is the realistic target unless Daniel's IEM duties match the GS-12 description.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) under Direct Hire Authority; no federal status or veterans' preference needed.

GS-11: one year of specialized experience at GS-09 equivalent (complex/sensitive issues, studies and responses to management on new requirements or regulations), or a Ph.D./3 years graduate education, or a combination with transcripts.

GS-12: one year of specialized experience at GS-11 equivalent (briefings, staff reports, recommendations to management, developing administrative procedures, interpreting guidelines and proposing policy).
No clearance required, but a pre-employment drug test and background checks apply; on-site in Arlington VA, Irving TX, or Washington DC with no telework.
strategy: Apply on October 30 or immediately after: only the first 150 applicants get first consideration, so have your resume and questionnaire answers ready before the posting opens.

Frame your IEM work in your own words around administrative and program-support tasks you actually did, such as government client deliverables, reports, briefings, logistics, budgets, procurement, or vendor coordination. Do not copy the announcement text, because the posting says copied language will not count.

For each job, list start and end dates (month/year), hours per week, and two to four specific bullets mapped to the GS-09/GS-11 specialized experience. Keep the resume within two pages, since only the first two pages are reviewed.
Highlight your policy knowledge as experience in interpreting regulations, legislation, and agency guidance and in drafting responses or recommendations for management or clients.

Answer the questionnaire honestly at the level your resume supports, since overstating can remove you from consideration. Prepare for the online competency assessment, which covers reasoning, reading comprehension, attention to detail, and similar areas.
Consider applying at GS-11 only, or at both grades if your duties clearly match GS-11 work. Upload transcripts if you have graduate coursework that could support a combination qualification.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [logistics/procurement/vendor] support for [number] [government client] engagements at IEM, managing [budget size or resources] and resolving [type of issue] to meet [deadline/requirement].

Drafted [briefings/status reports/recommendations] for [client or management audience] on [emergency management/recovery topic], interpreting [specific federal guidance, e.g., FEMA policy] to inform [decision or outcome].
Evaluated [process or system] and proposed [specific improvement], resulting in [measurable result you can verify].
interview_questions: Describe a time you identified an inefficiency in an administrative process and what you did to improve it.
Tell us about a time you had to interpret ambiguous guidelines or regulations to complete an assignment.
How have you managed relationships with vendors or with offices that controlled resources you needed?
Give an example of briefing a manager or client on a complex issue and the recommendation you made.
watch_outs: The application window is short (Oct 30–Nov 6, 2026), and the first 150 applicants receive priority, so applying late could mean you are never reviewed.
The duties are heavily operational (fleet, property, space, procurement), which is less policy- or public-facing than your strengths. Be sure the work appeals to you.
The role is fully on-site with no telework. Arlington or DC means a commute from Manassas, and the Irving, TX location would require relocation.
Qualifying depends on documenting a full year of experience at the right level. Vague IEM descriptions risk a not-qualified rating.
